blocs.texte: Un régime alimentaire équilibré (balanced diet) apporte au corps tous les nutriments nécessaires : protéines, glucides, matières grasses, vitamines, minéraux et fibres, en quantité raisonnable. La malbouffe (junk food) désigne les aliments riches en graisses, en sucre et en sel, mais pauvres en nutriments utiles.

Pour avoir une alimentation équilibrée, il faut consommer chaque jour : des fruits et légumes (vitamines et fibres), des féculents (glucides, énergie), des protéines (viande, poisson, œufs, légumineuses), des produits laitiers (calcium), et de l'eau en quantité suffisante. Il faut limiter le sucre, le sel et les graisses saturées présents dans la junk food.

A balanced meal could include: rice (carbohydrates), grilled fish (protein), steamed vegetables (vitamins and fibre), and a glass of water. In contrast, a typical junk food meal might include: a hamburger, French fries, and a sugary soft drink, which contain a lot of fat, salt and sugar but few essential nutrients.

blocs.enonce: Classe ces aliments en deux catégories : 'Healthy food' et 'Junk food' : rice, hamburger, fried chicken, vegetables, fruit, soft drink, fish, crisps (chips), water, candy.
blocs.solution: Healthy food: rice, vegetables, fruit, fish, water. Junk food: hamburger, fried chicken, soft drink, crisps (chips), candy.

blocs.texte: Me: Hi Poras, what do you usually eat for breakfast? Poras: I usually eat bread with butter and a cup of coffee. What about you? Me: I usually have rice with some vegetables. Poras: Really? That's quite unusual for breakfast! Do you eat junk food often? Me: Not very often, maybe once a week. I try to eat fruit instead of sweets. What about you? Poras: Honestly, I eat fast food quite often because it's quick and convenient. Me: You should be careful, too much junk food isn't good for your health. Poras: You're right. I should try to eat more balanced meals.

blocs.enonce: Réponds aux questions sur le dialogue : 1) What does Poras usually eat for breakfast? 2) What does 'me' usually have for breakfast? 3) How often does Poras eat fast food? 4) What advice does 'me' give to Poras?
blocs.solution: 1) He usually eats bread with butter and a cup of coffee. 2) He/She usually has rice with some vegetables. 3) He eats fast food quite often. 4) 'Me' advises Poras to be careful because too much junk food isn't good for his health, and to eat more balanced meals.

blocs.texte: 'Should' et 'shouldn't' s'utilisent pour donner un conseil, recommander ou déconseiller quelque chose.

Conseil positif : sujet + should + base verbale. Exemple : You should eat more vegetables. Conseil négatif : sujet + shouldn't (should not) + base verbale. Exemple : You shouldn't eat too much sugar. Question : Should + sujet + base verbale ? Exemple : Should I eat breakfast every day?

1) You should drink more water every day. 2) You shouldn't skip breakfast. 3) She should eat more fruit and vegetables. 4) They shouldn't eat fast food every day. 5) We should cook our meals at home more often.

blocs.enonce: Donne un conseil (should ou shouldn't) pour chaque situation : 1) Tom eats junk food every day. 2) Mary never drinks water, only soft drinks. 3) Paul skips breakfast every morning. 4) Lisa eats a lot of vegetables and fruit.
blocs.solution: 1) Tom shouldn't eat junk food every day. 2) Mary should drink more water instead of soft drinks. 3) Paul shouldn't skip breakfast. 4) Lisa should continue eating vegetables and fruit (bon exemple à suivre).

blocs.texte: Les adverbes de fréquence indiquent à quelle fréquence une action se produit. Ils se placent généralement avant le verbe principal, mais après le verbe 'to be'.

Avec un verbe ordinaire : sujet + adverbe + verbe. Exemple : I always eat breakfast. Avec le verbe 'to be' : sujet + to be + adverbe. Exemple : She is often late. Échelle de fréquence (du plus au moins fréquent) : always (100%) > usually > often > sometimes > rarely/seldom > never (0%).

1) I always eat vegetables with my meals. 2) She usually drinks tea in the morning. 3) We often eat rice for dinner. 4) He sometimes eats junk food. 5) They rarely eat sweets. 6) I never eat before going to bed.

blocs.enonce: Place correctement l'adverbe de fréquence dans la phrase : 1) I / eat / breakfast (always) 2) She / is / late (often) 3) We / drink / soft drinks (rarely) 4) He / is / hungry in the morning (never)
blocs.solution: 1) I always eat breakfast. 2) She is often late. 3) We rarely drink soft drinks. 4) He is never hungry in the morning.

blocs.texte: Le comparatif sert à comparer deux éléments, le superlatif sert à désigner l'élément qui se distingue le plus dans un groupe d'au moins trois éléments.

Adjectifs courts (1 syllabe) : comparatif = adjectif + ER + than (healthy → healthier than, attention au y → i). Superlatif = THE + adjectif + EST (the healthiest). Adjectifs longs (2 syllabes ou plus) : comparatif = MORE + adjectif + than (delicious → more delicious than). Superlatif = THE MOST + adjectif (the most delicious). Formes irrégulières : good → better → the best ; bad → worse → the worst.

1) Fruit is healthier than candy. 2) This restaurant is more expensive than that one. 3) Of all the dishes, this salad is the healthiest. 4) This is the most delicious cake I have ever eaten. 5) Home-cooked food is often better than fast food.

blocs.enonce: Complète avec le comparatif ou le superlatif de l'adjectif donné : 1) Vegetables are ... (healthy) than sweets. 2) This is ... (good) meal I have ever had. 3) Junk food is often ... (bad) for your health than home-cooked food. 4) Of all the fruits, mango is ... (delicious).
blocs.solution: 1) Vegetables are healthier than sweets. 2) This is the best meal I have ever had. 3) Junk food is often worse for your health than home-cooked food. 4) Of all the fruits, mango is the most delicious.

blocs.texte: 'But' et 'however' expriment un contraste entre deux idées. 'So' et 'therefore' expriment une conséquence.
1) Junk food is tasty, but it isn't healthy. 2) Junk food is tasty. However, it isn't healthy. 3) He ate too much sugar, so he felt sick. 4) He ate too much sugar. Therefore, he felt sick.

blocs.enonce: Relie les deux phrases avec le mot de liaison indiqué entre parenthèses : 1) Fast food is convenient. It is not nutritious. (but) 2) She eats a lot of vegetables. She stays healthy. (so) 3) Soft drinks are popular. They contain a lot of sugar. (however) 4) He skipped breakfast. He felt tired all morning. (therefore)
blocs.solution: 1) Fast food is convenient, but it is not nutritious. 2) She eats a lot of vegetables, so she stays healthy. 3) Soft drinks are popular. However, they contain a lot of sugar. 4) He skipped breakfast. Therefore, he felt tired all morning.
